findings.title: Renamed function breaks existing callers
findings.body: The function was renamed from `get_forecast` to `fetch_forecast`, but `weather/alerts.py` still imports and calls `get_forecast` on line 3. This will raise an `ImportError` for any code that depends on the old name. Either keep the original name or update all callers to use the new name.

findings.title: Inconsistent naming with local conventions
findings.body: The new function name `fetch_forecast` differs from the existing local convention in this file, where the function was previously named `get_forecast`. Renaming should follow a documented convention or be justified by a broader pattern. Consider aligning with the existing name unless there is a strong reason to change it.

summary.problem: Renaming `get_forecast` to `fetch_forecast` breaks existing callers and introduces inconsistency with local conventions.
summary.done_well: The function signature and logic remain unchanged, preserving the intended behavior.
